problem: After about six months he could not see the value of the college for its cost.
title: Steve Jobs drops out of college and drops in on a calligraphy class
context: Jobs attended Reed College, which was nearly as expensive as Stanford, using his working-class parents' savings.
decision_made: Drop out of Reed, and stay as a drop-in for about 18 more months, attending only classes that interested him.
action_taken: He sat in on a calligraphy course, which he later credited with the typography in personal computers.
observed_outcome: In a 2005 commencement speech Jobs argued that dropping in on the calligraphy class shaped the typography of personal computers, and said it was impossible to connect the dots looking forward.
lessons: Curiosity-driven choices can pay off in ways that cannot be planned, but the speaker's account is told with hindsight.
limitations: A single, self-told, retrospective account that fits a success story. It does not show that dropping out is a good choice for others, and many dropouts do not succeed.

claims.claim_text: Jobs dropped out of Reed College after about six months and stayed on as a drop-in.
Jobs said the calligraphy class he dropped in on influenced the typography of personal computers.
